learning_outcomes.text: To gain the ability to draw Free Body Diagrams and perform force analyses in mechanical system designs.
The student can find the resultant force and moment acting on a particle and a rigid body.
The student can find the reaction forces and moments acting on a rigid body.
To learn the theory and application of engineering mechanics applied to bodies under a three-dimensional force system.
Can calculate the center of gravity, center of mass, and geometric center of a particle or body.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to fundamental quantities and basic information of mechanics, Newton's Laws of Motion and Gravitation, a general guide to solving problems
Force Vectors, Force components, Parallelogram Law, determining the angle between two vectors or the projection of one vector onto another, scalar and vector products of force vectors
Equilibrium of particles, free body diagram
Force system, moment of a force, moment of a force about a specified axis
Calculation of support forces and moments on a body
Distributed Forces: Centroid and Center of Gravity
Calculation of resultant force and application point of distributed loads
Example Problem Solutions for Center of Gravity and Moments of Inertia
General Example Problem Solutions before Final Exam
assessment_rules: The midterm exam accounts for 40% of the grade, and the final exam accounts for 60%. Midterm and final exam dates are determined by the University Senate decisions in the academic calendar.
bibliography: Beer, F. P., Johnston, E. R., DeWolf, J. T., Mazurek, D. F., & Sanghi, S. (1992). Mechanics of materials (Vol. 1). New York: mcgraw-Hill.
